## Brand Strategy
- **Objective:** Increase ridership through coordinated system of information aids; increase public awareness of transit; make service easier to understand; integrate bus/rail interfaces.
- **Philosophy:** Simplification and consistency across all graphic applications. Systems approach to visual communications.
- **Design principles:** Brevity in messaging, adaptability to change, modular format, strict color/quality control.
- **Identity framework:** Uniform identity allowing individuality within a common framework across approximately 280 bus companies, commuter railroads, and port authorities.

## Logo
- **Logotype:** "NJ TRANSIT" -- NJ symbol interlocked with the word TRANSIT in Helvetica Medium all caps.
- **Symbol construction:** Built on a precise grid; height (X) is the basis for specifying size. NJ letters interlock. Symbol = 1/6 unit stroke width. Minimum size: 1/4" high.
- **Abbreviated version:** NJ symbol with "TRANSIT" below -- only where NJ TRANSIT identity is already well-established.
- **Slogan version:** For advertising/promotional printed applications only; never for identification applications. Minimum 6pt type for slogan legibility.
- **Reproduction rules:** Single color positive preferred (black on white default). Negative reproduction only on dark backgrounds or tinted glass. Logotype must never appear as a "stamp" in negative.
- **Signature:** Logotype combined with diagonal color stripe in prescribed proportions. On vehicles, logotype precedes stripe in direction of motion.

## Typography
- **Official typeface:** Helvetica Medium and Helvetica Regular, caps and lower case.
- **Usage:** Helvetica Medium for all type requirements except where Regular is noted (body copy). All sign messages in upper and lower case unless specified otherwise.
- **Spacing rules:** Normal letter spacing for all applications. Line spacing: 1.5x cap height for signs; 1pt leading for printed body copy. Word spacing: 3/4 cap height. Margins: minimum 3/4 of primary message cap height.
- **Schedule type sizes:** Headings 18pt Helvetica Medium; Body 10pt Helvetica Regular leaded 2pt; Timetable 6pt Regular leaded 0.8pt; Timepoints 6pt Medium leaded 1pt.

## Color
- **Thematic element:** Blue/Magenta/Orange diagonal stripe as unifying identity across all 2D and 3D applications.
- **Primary palette:**
  - Orange: PMS 165
  - Magenta: PMS 246
  - Blue: PMS Reflex Blue
  - White: DP 508-U (vehicles) / 3M 180-10 (signage)
  - Mineral Brown: PPG UC-50096 (street signage backgrounds, posts, hardware)
  - Rust Brown: PPG UC-50094 (rail station backgrounds, posts, hardware)
  - Black: PMS Opaque Black (printed applications dark field)
  - Red: PMS 485
  - Charcoal: DP 67259-U
  - Green: PMS 354
  - Stainless Steel Metallic: DP 826-A6-009
- **Cross-system specifications:** Pantone (printed), DuPont Imron (painted), 3M Scotchcal/Scotchlite (film), PPG Duracron (painted), Wornow (screened), plus industrial standard color manual references (Sherwin Williams, Moore, Benjamin, MAB).

## Graphics
- **Color stripe:** Three forms -- diagonal (unconstrained horizontal space), equal horizontal, unequal horizontal (constrained space).
- **Pictographs and symbols:** Modal (bus, bus stop, train, taxi, park-n-ride variants), regulatory (no smoking, no parking, no entry, handicapped), public services (men, women, toilets, elevator, first aid, ticket purchase, waiting area, telephone, information, restaurants, shops, lost and found, bag lockers, coffee shop, track crossing, concession). Aligned with US DOT symbol standards.
- **Arrows:** Standardized proportions; height varies by function (trailblazers: 2x cap height, vehicular: 1.5x, pedestrian: 1x).
- **Layout rules:** Printed materials flush left/ragged right. Signage: multiple messages flush left with arrow in left margin; single messages centered with arrow below.

## Photography
- Not applicable. This is an engineering/wayfinding-focused standards manual with no photography direction.

## Applications
- Extremely comprehensive across all transit touchpoints:
  - **Vehicles:** Specific bus models (GMC RTS-II, Flxible 870, GMC 4701), locomotives (GE F-40, GE U-34CH, GM E-8A), push-pull cars, Arrow rail cars, RDC-1, corporate sedans, vans, tow-wreckers.
  - **Signage:** Bus stops (basic, route ID, multi-operator, multi-route, major transfer, shelter, highway), trailblazers (park-n-ride, rail station, multi-mode), bus terminal identification, rail station signage (vehicular entrance, pedestrian, ticket windows, interior directional, platform, track crossing, system information display).
  - **Schedules:** Basic bus/train timetable, rider guides.
  - **Maps:** Rail system maps (geographic and schematic), single line route maps.
  - **Corporate forms:** Stationery, business cards.
- **Material specifications:** Aluminum sign panels, aluminum extrusions, steel posts, paint, screen process printing, decals/die-cut letters, reflective sheeting.

## Tone of Voice
- Purely functional/informational. No emotional or personality-driven language. Engineering precision in communication. Emphasis on brevity, clarity, and consistency for customer information.

## Outliers
- Historically significant document from 1981, scanned in 2022 -- represents a pivotal era in American transit identity design.
- Extraordinary scope: 169 pages covering everything from logo construction grids to specific vehicle models, material specs, and mounting hardware.
- Industrial color specifications across five different manufacturing systems (Pantone, DuPont, 3M, PPG, Wornow) with cross-reference tables.
- Legibility/distance formula: 1" cap height per 50 feet of viewing distance, with 75% retention at 45-degree viewing angle.
- Modular "changeability" system for updating signage via adhesive vinyl decals and mechanical composition adjustments.
- Signature rule: on vehicles, logotype must precede stripe in direction of motion -- rare kinetic identity consideration.
- Prepared under cooperative agreement between NJ DOT and Tri-State Regional Planning Commission.
- Peter Muller-Munk Associates is a historically notable industrial design firm.

## Quality Score
**5 / 5** -- A landmark transit graphics standards manual that is exhaustive in its engineering precision and comprehensive coverage. Every conceivable application is documented with exact specifications, from individual vehicle models to material fabrication standards. The cross-referencing system between graphic applications and material specifications is exemplary. A masterclass in systematic design thinking for complex multi-modal transit systems, and an important historical document in American transportation design.
